feedback.problem:
The entry ${a}_{32}^{′}$ in the inverse of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ k & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}]$
equals $1.$ Find the value of $k.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the determinant of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A)=|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ k & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}| & =1|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}|-(-1)|\begin{aligned}k & 0 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}|+0|\begin{aligned}k & 1 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-2-0)+(-2k-0)+0 \\  & =-2k-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we want the entry ${a}_{32}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need to know the value of ${c}_{23}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{23} & =(-1)^{2+3}|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(1-(-3)) \\  & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{32}^{′} & =\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{23} \\  & =\frac{1}{-2k-2}\cdot (-4) \\  & =\frac{2}{k+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since we are told that ${a}_{32}^{′}=1$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{k+1} & =1 \\ 2 & =k+1 \\ k & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
